subject.title: fix(cron): respect deliveryBestEffort in interim-message suppression guard

question: Should `deliveryBestEffort: true` override the descendant-related interim-message suppression guard and attempt delivery of acknowledgement-style output?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically small, but the flag’s intended scope is an operator-visible delivery policy: accepting this patch can make existing best-effort jobs emit messages that were formerly suppressed.

options.title: Treat best effort as delivery-first
options.body: Merge the proposed exemption so best-effort jobs attempt delivery even when the available output matches an interim hint and descendant state exists.

options.title: Preserve interim filtering
options.body: Keep the current suppression behavior and define interim-message filtering as an intentional exception to best-effort delivery.

options.title: Define a separate policy
options.body: Keep the current behavior until maintainers choose a separately named setting for operators who want acknowledgement-style messages delivered.

recommendation.title: Treat best effort as delivery-first
recommendation.body: Merge the proposed exemption so best-effort jobs attempt delivery even when the available output matches an interim hint and descendant state exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent cron-delivery work is the strongest available history signal for the `deliveryBestEffort` semantics.
